fit: fig fruit oral challenge and acute allergic symptoms
assessment: Two allergy cases had oral then respiratory symptoms on challenge. Skin showed stronger allergenicity than pulp in study tests. The author abstract gives no separate drooling measurement, and full case histories remain open.

fit: Parkinson drooling and perioral dermatitis in a clinical case
assessment: The authors describe worse chronic drooling and skin damage, followed by secretion suppression and skin improvement after salivary-gland treatment. No raw fig or graded dietary response.

fit: Parkinson dysphagia and oral levodopa transport in one person
assessment: The case reports higher drug concentration and improved swallowing on repeat testing after tongue training. Jelly composition is unspecified and both tests used it. There is no isolated fig or formal drooling result.

fit: food-frequency questionnaire and sialorrhea scale in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: Separate dietary and drooling measures were collected. The article and 111-page supplement include grouped fruit measures, with no named raw-fig comparison or fig-specific drooling estimate. Full clinical links and item metadata are restricted.

fit: pooled randomized amantadine trials and item 2.2
assessment: At week 12 MDS-UPDRS item 2.2 numerically favored amantadine without a statistically clear contrast. Exploratory threshold shifts and the overall comparison use different summaries. No fig was assigned.

fit: separate measures of Parkinson drooling and saliva output
assessment: The Parkinson group had more drooling and lower average stimulated and unstimulated saliva flow than matched controls. The printed unstimulated median conflicts with its mean and range. No raw-fig exposure in the study; the scope is clinical measurement.

fit: separate sialorrhea and swallowing scales in Parkinson restless-legs groups
assessment: Drooling scores did not clearly differ (3.56 versus 3.88, P=.561), while swallowing-disturbance scores differed. Restless legs status supplies the comparison rather than a culinary exposure.
